title: Jesse Price, Jimmy King, Freddie Jenkins; players who started on drums
summary: Jones remembers Jesse Price, Jimmy King and Freddie Jenkins and notes that Roy Eldridge and Harry James began on drums.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: There was one drummer that could have been and should have been. That was Jesse Price. Just straight jazz. I tried to show him for 6 long months, Milt, how to play vibraphones, "Trees", just "Trees" in the key of B-flat. He'd fix pork chops and eggs for me and I'd be laying on the bed and telling him what note to hit. He was just too thick - we called him "Country" but he's a beautiful man and a natural. When you speak about the musical drummers, the top great musical drummer I knew was a fellow by the name of Jimmy King that was short lived. He died in the 20's. He was with Rex Stewart; he played with the Wilberforce Collegians. Rex was in the band. Horace Henderson had the band, which was a great penman, you know, he was a great penman. Then we had a little fellow by the name of Freddie Jenkins that put the flash in jazz. Freddie Jenkins was a trumpet player that later went with Duke. He had an accident with his fingers. But you must remember most of these guys started on drums and went to the trumpet like Roy did -
You mean Roy Eldridge started on drums?
Roy Eldridge on drums, yes. Like Harry James, he started on drums.
